mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI engine typically costs £1,800-£2,800 supply-only, depending on which generation and engine code your car has. OM640.940 (W245, 2.0L) and OM651.901 (W246, 1.8L) are priced similarly for rebuilt units. Used engine: £900-£1,600 depending on mileage and condition. Reconditioned engine: £1,500-£2,400. Rebuilt engine: £1,800-£2,800 with 12-month warranty. Fitting adds £400-£800 at a specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning sign on OM651.901 (W246) B180 CDI engines is a rattling noise on cold start, lasting 1-3 seconds. This indicates the timing chain tensioner is losing hydraulic pressure. Rattling on cold start - the first and most important warning sign. Engine management light with P0016 or P0017 camshaft/crankshaft correlation codes. Loss of power, misfire or rough running. Complete failure leads to chain snap, bent valves and catastrophic engine damage. Warning: Ignoring cold-start rattle on an OM651.901 leads to chain snap, bent valves, and a £3,000+ repair bill. Replace the tensioner preventatively.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI have a timing chain or belt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the OM640.940 (W245, 2005-2011) and OM651.901 (W246, 2011-2018) engines in the Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI use a timing chain, not a belt. The OM651.901 chain is located at the rear of the engine (gearbox side), making replacement more labour-intensive than a conventional front-chain layout. OM640.940: single roller chain, front-mounted. OM651.901: single roller chain, rear-mounted. Neither engine has a cambelt - no scheduled replacement interval, but tensioner wear is common. Cold-start rattle = tensioner warning - act immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a high-mileage Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: For W245 models (2005-2011) worth £1,500-£3,500, a rebuilt engine at £1,800-£2,800 often approaches the car's value. However, if the body and transmission are sound, specialist replacement with 12-month warranty can still be cheaper than buying a comparable replacement car. W246 models (2011-2018, worth £4,000-£8,000) are almost always worth repairing. W245 (2005-2011): value £1.5k-£3.5k - borderline economical, evaluate carefully. W246 (2011-2018): value £4k-£8k - replacement makes sense. Rebuilt engine (£1.8k-£2.8k fitted) often cheaper than comparable replacement car. Factory-quality rebuild with upgraded components often outlasts original.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Well-maintained OM640.940 and OM651.901 diesel engines regularly reach 180,000-250,000 miles with proper servicing. Timing chain tensioner issues on OM651 are the main factor limiting longevity if not addressed preventatively. OM640.940 (W245): 180,000-250,000 miles; injector and turbo failures the main limiters. OM651.901 (W246): 180,000-250,000 miles; timing chain tensioner the primary concern. Regular oil changes (every 10,000 miles or annually) essential for both. Short-trip driving kills DPF - use for longer journeys where possible.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the B180 CDI and B200 CDI engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B180 CDI and B200 CDI share the same engine family in each generation but are tuned differently. In the W245 (OM640), the B180 CDI produces 109bhp while the B200 CDI produces 140bhp from the same 2.0L displacement. In the W246 (OM651.901 vs OM651.930), the B180 CDI delivers 109bhp from 1.8L while the B200 CDI produces 136bhp. Same engine family, different state of tune. B180 CDI: lower power, better fuel economy (50-54mpg). B200 CDI: higher power, slightly worse economy. Replacement engines are not interchangeable without ECU remapping.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI entered the UK market in September 2005 as the entry-level diesel in the first-generation W245 range. Powered initially by a 2.0-litre OM640.940 diesel producing 109bhp, the B180 CDI was repositioned in 2011 with the second-generation W246, switching to the 1.8-litre OM651.901 BlueEFFICIENCY unit while retaining the same power output but with improved fuel economy and lower emissions.

milestones.description: September 2005 - W245 launch: OM640.940 2.0L diesel, 109bhp, 250Nm torque, Euro 4 emissions
July 2005 - Diesel Particulate Filter becomes standard equipment from this date
W245 facelift: cosmetic updates only; engine range unchanged
November 2011 - W246 launch: OM651.901 1.8L diesel BlueEFFICIENCY, 109bhp, 250Nm torque, Euro 5 emissions
W246 facelift: OM651.901 continues, revised styling and interior updates

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI is broadly reliable, but both engine families - the OM640.940 in W245 cars and the OM651.901 in W246 models - have well-documented failure points. Timing chain tensioner issues dominate OM651 enquiries, while injector and turbo failures affect higher-mileage OM640 units. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI OM651.901 Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI (OM651.901, 2011-2018, W246)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner loses hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack and guide rail fracture. On OM651 diesels, the chain is located at the rear of the engine (gearbox side), requiring gearbox removal for replacement. A rattling noise on cold start is the first warning sign.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, tensioner and guides. No engine removal.
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-80k miles if caught early. Suitable only before chain jumps or guides fail.

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Chain Failure With Valve Damage
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove cylinder head, replace bent valves, guides, full timing set, head gasket.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if no piston or bore damage. Labour-intensive.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of fully rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components, bench tested, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when damage extends to pistons, bearings or cylinder head.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W246 Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI (2011-2018) is worth approximately £4,000-£8,000 depending on mileage and condition. W245 models (2005-2011) are typically £1,500-£3,500. If your OM651.901 engine has suffered timing chain failure with valve damage, a specialist full engine replacement at £1,800-£2,800 is often more cost-effective than a dealer head rebuild exceeding £3,500 - and delivers a fresh warranty.
problems.recommendation: On a W246 B180 CDI, if you hear chain rattle on cold start but the engine still runs smoothly, a specialist preventative chain replacement (£900-£1,400) is excellent value. If the chain has already jumped and valves are bent, compare rebuilt engine prices - a specialist fitted unit at £1,800-£2,800 often costs less than a dealer head rebuild and delivers a fresh warranty.

problems.h4: Injector Failure - Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI OM640.940 Diesel Misfire & Hard Start
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI (OM640.940, 2005-2011, W245)
problems.rootCause: Injector coil pack failure, seal leakage or carbon buildup around the injector nozzle causes misfire, rough idle, excessive smoke and hard starting when hot. Injector failure can lead to bore wash, damaging piston rings and cylinder bores.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace one faulty injector with genuine or OEM-spec unit. Relearn via diagnostics.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable when only one injector fails and others test within spec.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all four injectors, copper seals, leak-off lines. Full coding and adaptation.
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when multiple injectors failing or high mileage.

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt Engine With Upgraded Injectors
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with new injectors, timing components and warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if bore wash from leaking injectors has damaged piston rings or bores.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: W245 B180 CDI values are now £1,500-£3,500. A dealer full replacement exceeding £5,500 is rarely justified. If your OM640 engine has injector knock and bore wash is suspected, a specialist fitted rebuilt engine at £1,800-£2,800 delivers a fresh engine with new injectors and a 12-month warranty for less than a dealer injector-plus-labour repair.
problems.recommendation: Single injector failure is common on OM640 engines beyond 100,000 miles. A specialist replacement at £350-£500 is straightforward. However, if you're experiencing hard start when hot plus misfire and smoke, multiple injectors are likely failing - a full set replacement at £1,100-£1,600 is more cost-effective than repeated single swaps. Only consider engine replacement if injector failure has caused bore wash or the engine has other major issues.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM640.940 injector replacement and rebuilt engines for your B180 CDI

problems.h4: DPF & EGR Cooler Blockage - Mercedes-Benz B Class B180 CDI Emissions & Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: On both OM640 and OM651 engines, DPF blockages are common in vehicles used for short trips or urban driving, where the filter cannot regenerate properly. Soot accumulates, triggering warning lights, reduced performance and increased fuel consumption. Early W245 OM640 cars without DPF (pre-July 2005) are less affected, but post-July 2005 cars and all W246 models have DPF systems.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cracked EGR cooler, flush coolant, reset adaptations.
repairOptions.longevity: Essential first step if white smoke and coolant loss present.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Professional DPF off-car clean or replacement, new EGR valve/cooler, forced regeneration.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable when DPF is clogged but not melted or cracked.

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt Engine With New Emissions Components
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with new EGR cooler, DPF, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required when DPF is melted, turbo damaged or engine has multiple failures.

problems.recommendation: On a B180 CDI beyond 80,000 miles, regular motorway driving helps the DPF regenerate naturally - short-trip cars are most at risk. If your DPF is clogged but not melted, an off-car professional clean (£700-£1,100) restores function. If the car has been driven in limp mode for extended periods, the DPF and turbo may be beyond repair - at that stage, a rebuilt engine with new emissions components is the only reliable long-term solution.
